summary:
Forbidden But Not Forgotten

Project Overview

Forbidden But Not Forgotten is an interactive space museum dedicated to humanity’s exploration of the Moon and Mars. It preserves and presents the stories of spacecraft, scientific instruments, and equipment left behind by past missions.

Main Features

- Planetary Exploration: Explore interactive representations of the Moon and Mars.
- Mission Locations: Discover landing sites and their historical significance through interactive maps.
- Three-Dimensional Models: Examine detailed models of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments.
- Mission Histories: Learn about each mission’s objectives, achievements, and lasting contributions.
- Historical Timeline: Trace the development of lunar and Martian exploration over time.

Information Sources

- NASA
- ESA
- ISRO
- CNSA
- UAE Space Agency

Project Goal

The project transforms the history of lunar and Martian exploration into an engaging educational experience. It enables users to discover abandoned objects and understand their scientific, technological, and historical significance.

Project Vision

We explore not only the planets themselves, but also humanity’s enduring legacy beyond Earth.

Forbidden But Not Forgotten: Every object has a story, and every mission leaves a legacy.
details: Forbidden But Not Forgotten – Project Details Forbidden But Not Forgotten is an interactive educational space museum that explores the objects, spacecraft, scientific instruments, and equipment left behind during human exploration of the Moon and Mars. What does the project do, and how does it work? The project provides users with an interactive website where they can explore the Moon and Mars and discover the history of different space missions. Users can select mission locations on interactive planetary surfaces to access information about the missions, the equipment involved, its original purpose, and its contribution to space exploration. The experience also incorporates 3D models that help users visualize spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments. Instead of presenting information as ordinary text, the project combines interactive exploration, visual storytelling, historical information, and 3D technology to make learning more engaging. What benefits does it have? - Makes space exploration history easier and more interesting to understand. - Preserves information about equipment and spacecraft left behind on the Moon and Mars. - Helps students and space enthusiasts learn about scientific missions and their achievements. - Connects historical events with the locations and objects associated with them. - Provides an interactive educational experience rather than relying only on traditional articles and images. What is the intended impact? Our goal is to raise awareness of the history and legacy of space exploration. Many people know about famous missions, but fewer know about the objects and scientific equipment that remain on planetary surfaces after those missions. We want users to understand that every object has a purpose, every mission has a story, and even equipment that is no longer active can have lasting scientific and historical importance. The project aims to make this information accessible to a wider audience and encourage curiosity about planetary science, engineering, and future space exploration. What tools, programming languages, and software were used? The project was developed as a web-based application using: - HTML5 – for the website structure. - CSS3 – for the visual design, layouts, animations, and responsive interface. - JavaScript – for interactive features and application logic. - Three.js – for rendering and displaying interactive 3D planetary environments and models. - GLB 3D models – for displaying selected spacecraft and scientific equipment. - NASA and other space agency resources – for researching mission histories, locations, and scientific information. Development and testing were carried out using a Windows-based computer and a web browser. How is the project creative and innovative? The creative aspect of Forbidden But Not Forgotten is its approach to space exploration. Most educational platforms focus on the missions themselves, but our project focuses on what those missions left behind. We transform mission data and historical information into an interactive digital museum. Users can explore planetary surfaces, select mission locations, view 3D objects, and discover the stories behind them. This combination of planetary exploration, interactive maps, 3D visualization, and historical storytelling creates a different way to experience the history of space exploration. What factors did our team consider? During development, we considered several important factors: - Scientific accuracy: Using reliable information from recognized space agencies and research resources. - User experience: Making navigation simple and allowing users to explore information naturally. - Performance: Keeping 3D models and visual assets optimized so the website can run on a range of devices. - Accessibility: Presenting scientific information in a clear and understandable way. - Educational value: Making sure that each interactive element helps users learn something meaningful. - Historical preservation: Distinguishing between active missions, completed missions, and equipment that remains on planetary surfaces. Ultimately, Forbidden But Not Forgotten is designed to turn the forgotten remains of space exploration into an accessible digital experience that connects science, technology, history, and education.
